name: Pickle Robot truck unloader
summary: A mobile unloading robot for trailers and ocean containers: an industrial arm with suction gripping on a base that moves deeper into the trailer by itself and puts floor-loaded boxes of up to 50 lb onto an onboard conveyor. UPS uses it in the US.

germany.statusNote: No German or EU sales route found; Pickle Robot (Charlestown, Massachusetts) sells and installs in the US via "Schedule a call" on its website.

specs.label: Max box weight
specs.quote: weighs up to 50lbs for loose packed, floor loaded freight

specs.label: Box sizes
specs.value: 6 x 6 x 6 in up to 24 x 24 x 32 in
specs.quote: Handles packages from 6" x 6" x 6" cubes up to 24" x 24" x 32"

specs.label: Unloading rate
specs.conditions: dependent on freight, in production deployments
specs.quote: Systems reliably achieve 400-1,500 PPH (dependent on freight) in production deployments

specs.label: Trailers and containers
specs.value: Any length standard-height road trailers; standard and high-cube ocean containers
specs.quote: Works in any length, standard height, over the road trailers and both standard height and high cube ocean containers.

specs.label: Set-up
specs.value: Moves dock to dock, sets up in under 5 minutes; in production in under 5 days
specs.quote: Moves dock to dock. Sets up in under 5 minutes.

specs.label: Arm
specs.value: One KUKA industrial arm with suction gripper, onboard conveyor
specs.quote: The system uses KUKA robot arms and works with commercially available conveyors.

notes: Arm payload is the stated maximum box weight (50 lb = about 22.7 kg).
Works at the dock door: the base drives into the trailer as it empties; no WMS integration needed according to the maker.
The mobile base is taken as wheeled; its drive type is not described in the pages read.

evidence.task: Unloads floor-loaded parcels from trailers at UPS facilities
evidence.note: UPS statement on the maker's home page: "UPS is using Pickle Robot’s unloading technologies to ease the challenging job of unloading trailers".

evidence.task: UPS plans to buy about 400 truck-unloading robots for about 120 million USD
evidence.note: Based on Bloomberg reporting; a purchase plan, roll-out dates not in the article.
